conventions: בֵּית מְרִי as a predicate (3.9, 3.26, 3.27): the construct בַּיִת takes the construction-supplied copula *are* together with the indefinite article of its phrase (rules 20, 15), מְרִי takes the attributive *rebellious* (rule 28), and the explicit הֵמָּה takes only *they* (rule 20). Where an explicit subject noun stands in the clause instead, as at 3.7 (*all the house of Israel are of a hard forehead*), the resumptive הֵמָּה is unrepresented under rule 22 and the copula still goes to the predicate.

הַמְּגִלָּה הַזֹּאת (3.1, 3.2, 3.3): the ASV writes exactly one determiner for the phrase. Where that word is *this*, the demonstrative pronoun licenses it and both articles go unrepresented (3.1, 3.3); where it is *the*, the first article takes it and the demonstrative goes unrepresented (3.2). The agreement article standing on the demonstrative is never the morpheme that takes a written determiner.

The זָהַר family (3.17-3.21): where the ASV writes a light verb plus complement — *give warning*, *givest warning*, *hast given warning*, *took warning* — the whole rendering is that verb's one unit headed on *warning* (rule 44), discontinuous around an object pronoun, which belongs to the object suffix under rule 18. Where the ASV writes a single *warn*, the verb takes that word and nothing more.

The object marker אֵת is unrepresented on every bare object in this chapter (rule 16) and takes English only where the ASV's verb of speaking reaches its object through *with*: 3.22 *talk with thee*, 3.24 *spake with me*, 3.27 *speak with thee* (rule 16, first family). The אֵת of 3.3 is not the marker at all: MACULA tags it R, so it is the homograph preposition H854 aligning as an ordinary preposition. Read the morphology, not the '(et)' gloss.

אָבָה before לְ + infinitive (3.7, twice): the ASV's *will not hearken* puts *will* on אָבָה — the finite verb in the first clause, the participle under אֵין in the second — and the lexical verb on the infinitive, while the לְ is unrepresented for want of a written complementizer (rules 40, 52). Do not read *will* as the infinitive's own auxiliary under rule 17; the verb of willing is what it renders, as rule 35 reads a modal onto יָכֹל where that verb stands in the clause.
report: Checked all 57 candidate lemmas and read the 27-verse dump end to end for the added-unit splits the table is blind to. Every difference the table surfaces is one the ASV licenses; no construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license it. verdict no-change, patches empty.

The demonstrative phrase הַמְּגִלָּה הַזֹּאת (3.1, 3.2, 3.3) is consistent, not split. The ASV writes one determiner for the phrase: it goes to the demonstrative pronoun where that word is *this* (3.1, 3.3 — both articles unrepresented) and to the first article where it is *the* (3.2 — demonstrative unrepresented). Rules 41 and 47 decide all three the same way, and the agreement article on the demonstrative never takes it.

רָשָׁע / צַדִּיק look like two analyses and are not. Where an article morpheme stands (3.18 [הַ]רָשָׁע → *the wicked*) the article takes the written *the* and the unit heads on it (rules 12, 15); where none stands (3.18 s018, 3.19, 3.20, 3.21) the substantive takes the supplied *the* or *a* into its own unit and heads on the adjective (rules 46, 31). Presence of the morpheme is exactly what selects the rule.

זָהַר (7 occurrences, 5 treatments) is coherent: *give / givest / hast given / took warning* are light verb plus complement headed on *warning* (rule 44) in 3.17, 3.18, 3.20, 3.21, with any object suffix taking the pronoun inside the rendering; a single written *warn* keeps the verb whole in 3.18 (infinitive), 3.19 and 3.21. The waws are the same story: וְלֹא fuses to *neither* / *nor* in 3.9 and 3.18, while the bare waw of 3.19 takes *nor* on a negative gapped from the previous line — rule 35 applied in both directions.

The four added units each survive the subtraction test against every morpheme that could have carried them. 3.3 *it*: the Sh token is a cohortative he (rule 32) and no object morpheme is present, so the pronoun joins nothing (rules 30, 44). 3.5 *but*: no waw or other conjunction stands in the clause, and the negative and אֶל already have their own renderings (rules 51, 55) — this is the chapter's only conjunctionless contrastive, every other *But / Yet / Nevertheless* having a waw. 3.12 *saying* and 3.13 *I heard*: italicised, with no verb of speaking or hearing in the Hebrew (rules 7, 20, 30).

The object marker is unrepresented on all eight bare objects and takes English only in 3.22, 3.24 and 3.27, where the ASV's verb of speaking reaches its object through *with* (rule 16, first family). The אֵת of 3.3 is MACULA-tagged R — the homograph preposition H854 — and that verse already records the correction; the display gloss '(et)' contradicts the morphology and is not evidence (rule 39).

BSB: none of the 23 disagreements is a genuine error. The Td × 7 block is the demonstrative-phrase and agreement articles (rules 41, 47); the To block is rule 16; the R × 5 block is the unrendered לְ of an infinitive and of לֵאמֹר plus two rule-40 bare-object recastings (3.3 *give thee*, 3.11 *tell them*); הֵמָּה 3.7 and the suffix of Adonai in 3.11/3.27 are rule 22. Two are judgment rather than convention and both are already documented in their verses: 3.15 אֵשֵׁב, a whole verb left unrepresented because the ASV recasts the following clause locatively as *and to where they dwelt* and renders the verb once at s019; and 3.21 וֹ, an object suffix rendered once by the appositional *the righteous man*. Neither warrants a change, and no edge was touched to improve the 96.2% figure.

Five conventions recorded against an empty log; no contract promotion. The chapter met no rule's unconsidered case — the אָבָה + infinitive reading of 3.7 is recorded as a chapter convention rather than promoted, since two units of one lemma in one chapter is thin evidence for a rule that would bind every chapter after this one.
